baseline: Host Linux 6.8.0-124-generic, prebuilt semget02 from LTP 20260529 (/nix/store/hik6kb512ia3p14lc2vwzb292d4k306a-ltp-20260529, copied to /tmp/ltpbase/bin before running so nothing was written inside the store): 6 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken. setup() creates the set with semget(semkey, 10, IPC_CREAT|IPC_EXCL) so its stored mode is 0 (no permission bits) and its uid/gid/cuid/cgid are root's euid/egid. Per assertion, with PSEMS=10, SEM_RA=0600, SEMMSL=32000 (matches host /proc/sys/kernel/sem): (1) semget(semkey, 10, 0600) from a child that has setuid'd to nobody (uid 65534) on an existing root-owned mode-0 set => -1/EACCES(13); (2) semget(semkey, 10, IPC_CREAT|IPC_EXCL) as root, key exists => -1/EEXIST(17); (3) semget(semkey1, 10, 0600) as root, no set for that key and no IPC_CREAT => -1/ENOENT(2); (4) semget(semkey1, -1, IPC_CREAT|IPC_EXCL) => -1/EINVAL(22); (5) semget(semkey1, 32001, IPC_CREAT|IPC_EXCL) => -1/EINVAL(22); (6) semget(semkey, 11, 0600) as root, existing set holds 10 semaphores => -1/EINVAL(22). Only assertion 1 exercises IPC permission; the other five are argument/existence validation and all run as root, which in Linux short-circuits the permission test via CAP_IPC_OWNER regardless.
failing_assertion: semget02.c:53, subtest 1: 'TFAIL: semget(1627851663, 10, 384) succeeded'. Asterinas returned a valid positive semaphore id from sys_semget where the correct value is -1 with errno EACCES. Asterinas scores 5 passed / 1 failed against the host's 6/6; the other five subtests produce byte-identical result lines (EEXIST(17), ENOENT(2), EINVAL(22), EINVAL(22), EINVAL(22)). The child's SAFE_SETUID(65534) succeeded, so the failure is the permission decision and not a credentials-transition problem.
root_cause: IpcNamespace::validate_sem_set (kernel/src/ipc/ipc_ns.rs:177-184) is a stub: it binds the semaphore set as `_sem_set` and never reads it, emits warn!("Semaphore doesn't support permission check now") when the requested mode is non-empty, and returns Ok(()) unconditionally. It is the only permission gate in the SysV IPC code, so no IPC permission check exists anywhere in the kernel. get_or_create_sem_set reaches it at line 145 on the existing-key path. The set's stored credentials are correct and sufficient to decide the case: sys_semget computes mode = semflg & 0x1FF (kernel/src/syscall/semget.rs:9), which is 0 for the IPC_CREAT|IPC_EXCL used in setup, and SemaphoreSet::new builds IpcPermission::new_sem_perm(key, credentials.euid(), credentials.egid(), mode) (kernel/src/ipc/semaphore/system_v/sem_set.rs:251-252), so the set is mode 0 owned by uid 0. When the nobody child calls semget, line 136 finds the set, line 137 confirms the key matches, line 145 calls the stub which returns Ok, line 147 is skipped because IPC_CREAT|IPC_EXCL is absent, line 154 passes because num_sems() (10) is not less than the requested 10, and line 158 returns Ok(semid) - the wrong success the test observes. A second defect sits at the same call site: line 145 hardcodes `PermissionMode::ALTER | PermissionMode::READ` rather than deriving the requested access from the caller's semflg the way Linux does (requested_mode = (flag>>6)|(flag>>3)|flag), so the requested permission is independent of semflg. A third divergence is ordering: Asterinas checks permission at 145 before the IPC_EXCL test at 147-152 and the nsems test at 154-156, whereas ipcget_public tests EEXIST first, then more_checks, then permission last. That ordering is invisible to semget02 (its non-EACCES subtests all run as root) but combined with the hardcoded ALTER|READ it would make an unprivileged IPC_CREAT|IPC_EXCL against an existing mode-0 set return EACCES where Linux returns EEXIST. Ruled out as a cause: the semid = key % SEMMNI + 1 hash at line 133 does not collide here. SEMMNI is 32000 (sem_set.rs:20), the two ftok keys differ only in the proj byte, and (1<<24) % 32000 = 9216 != 0, so keys from one directory can never map to the same slot; the observed run used 1627851663 and 1644628879 and subtests 3-5 returned ENOENT/EINVAL rather than the ENOSPC that a collision produces at line 140.
invariant: Access to an already-existing System V IPC object must be authorized against that object's stored ownership and mode before a handle to it is returned to the caller. The access bits the caller requests, folded from its flag argument into a single owner/group/other triplet, must be a subset of the one triplet of the object's mode selected by the caller's credentials: the owner triplet when the caller's effective uid equals the object's owner or creator uid, otherwise the group triplet when the object's owner or creator gid is one of the caller's groups, otherwise the other triplet. A caller holding CAP_IPC_OWNER in the object's user namespace is exempt. Creating a new object carries no such check, because there is no pre-existing owner to consult.
owning_layer: The shared System V IPC permission layer: the IpcPermission type in kernel/src/ipc/mod.rs (lines 57-112), with the predicate invoked from IpcNamespace in kernel/src/ipc/ipc_ns.rs where the validate_sem_set stub sits today. This is the closest Asterinas equivalent to Linux's ipcperms(). It must not live in SemaphoreSet or in the individual sys_sem* handlers: the rule is byte-identical for message queues and shared memory, which ipc_ns.rs's own module documentation says 'remain to be added', and IpcPermission is already the single type that all three object kinds are meant to share - it stores key/uid/gid/cuid/cguid/mode and nothing semaphore-specific. Putting the check on IpcPermission means the future msgget and shmget lookup paths inherit it instead of each re-deriving it, which is exactly the recurrence this field exists to prevent. PermissionMode (kernel/src/ipc/semaphore/system_v/mod.rs:10-16: ALTER=0o002, WRITE=0o002, READ=0o004) is already expressed in Linux's folded low-three-bit form, so it is the correct argument type for the requested mode, though it currently lives under semaphore/system_v and would want to move up alongside IpcPermission for msg/shm to reuse.
linux_reference: ipcperms() in ipc/util.c:553-573 (v6.8, read from source). Its placement is the point: it lives in the shared IPC utility file, not in sem.c, msg.c or shm.c. Body: requested_mode = (flag >> 6) | (flag >> 3) | flag; granted_mode = ipcp->mode; granted_mode >>= 6 if uid_eq(current_euid(), ipcp->cuid) || uid_eq(current_euid(), ipcp->uid), else granted_mode >>= 3 if in_group_p(ipcp->cgid) || in_group_p(ipcp->gid); then fail if (requested_mode & ~granted_mode & 0007) && !ns_capable(ns->user_ns, CAP_IPC_OWNER). On the semget path it is called from ipc_check_perms() (util.c:365-381), which maps its failure to -EACCES, itself called from ipcget_public() (util.c:397-433) in this order: ipc_findkey, then -EEXIST when IPC_CREAT|IPC_EXCL, then ops->more_checks (sem_more_checks in ipc/sem.c returns -EINVAL when params->u.nsems > sma->sem_nsems), then ipc_check_perms last. ksys_semget (ipc/sem.c) rejects nsems < 0 || nsems > ns->sc_semmsl with -EINVAL before ipcget is entered, and ipcget() dispatches IPC_PRIVATE to ipcget_new() -> newary(), which performs no permission check at all. Asterinas already matches Linux on how the object is stamped: newary sets sma->sem_perm.mode = semflg & S_IRWXUGO (sem.c:549) and ipc_addid sets cuid = uid = euid, gid = cgid = egid (util.c). Two details worth copying that are easy to get wrong: the uid comparison uses current_euid() while the group comparison uses in_group_p(), which tests cred->fsgid first and only then searches the supplementary group set (kernel/groups.c), so the two halves read different credential fields; and when neither owner nor group matches, granted_mode is deliberately left unshifted so the trailing & 0007 selects the 'other' triplet. Beyond semget, sem.c calls ipcperms directly at lines 1263, 1368, 1425 and 2061, i.e. for semctl GETALL/SETVAL/SETALL and for semop with alter ? S_IWUGO : S_IRUGO.
other_callers: Not narrow - every semaphore syscall Asterinas implements reaches this defect, so all of them are fixed or missed together. sys_semctl (kernel/src/syscall/semctl.rs) already passes meaningful modes into the stub: PermissionMode::READ for IPC_STAT, SEM_GETPID, SEM_GETVAL, SEM_GETNCNT and SEM_GETZCNT (lines 53, 62, 72, 79, 86) and PermissionMode::ALTER for SEM_SETVAL (line 96). All six are unchecked today, which means any process can read or overwrite the values of any semaphore set in the namespace; de-stubbing validate_sem_set fixes all six with no call-site change. sys_semop (kernel/src/ipc/semaphore/system_v/sem.rs:212 and 289) is the exception that needs its own edit: it passes PermissionMode::empty() and carries a matching TODO at lines 199-200 ('Semaphore operation doesn't support permission check now'), so even a correct predicate would authorize nothing. Linux checks alter ? S_IWUGO : S_IRUGO there (sem.c:2061), and sem.rs has already computed is_alter at line 197, so the call site must pass ALTER or READ. sys_semctl(IPC_RMID) (semctl.rs:36-51) bypasses validate_sem_set entirely and hand-rolls euid == uid || euid == cuid with its own TODO about capabilities; Linux enforces a different rule for that operation (util.c:449-465, which also admits CAP_SYS_ADMIN), so it is a related but separate gap and not something this fix should silently absorb. Message queues and shared memory have no implementation yet, so nothing there is broken today - but they are precisely why the predicate belongs on IpcPermission rather than in semaphore code.
suggested_direction: Add the predicate to IpcPermission in kernel/src/ipc/mod.rs, e.g. `fn check_access(&self, requested: PermissionMode, credentials: &Credentials<ReadOp>) -> Result<()>`, mirroring ipcperms(): pick the granted triplet by shifting mode right 6 when credentials.euid() equals self.uid() or self.cuid(), else right 3 when self.gid() or self.cguid() matches credentials.fsgid() or is present in credentials.groups(), else leave it unshifted; then return EACCES when `requested.bits() & !granted & 0o7 != 0`. All the inputs already exist - static_cap.rs exposes euid(), egid(), fsgid() and groups() (a BTreeSet<Gid>), and IpcPermission already stores every field needed. The CAP_IPC_OWNER escape needs the namespace-scoped hook already used at ipc_ns.rs:85: lsm_hooks::on_capable(CapableContext::new(self.owner.as_ref(), posix_thread, CapSet::IPC_OWNER)) - CapSet::IPC_OWNER is defined at kernel/src/process/credentials/capabilities.rs:26 and currently unused. That is the one structural cost: validate_sem_set is a static fn today, and it needs &self (for owner) plus the caller's PosixThread/Credentials, so with_sem_set must thread those through from its five semctl call sites and two sem.rs call sites. Then, at the semget site: (1) replace the hardcoded PermissionMode::ALTER | PermissionMode::READ at ipc_ns.rs:145 with the fold of the caller's mode bits, ((mode >> 6) | (mode >> 3) | mode) & 0o7 - `mode` is already a parameter of get_or_create_sem_set; (2) move that check below the IPC_EXCL test at 147-152 and the num_sems test at 154-156 so the error precedence matches ipcget_public; (3) in sem.rs:212 pass `if is_alter { PermissionMode::ALTER } else { PermissionMode::READ }` and delete the TODO at 199-200, leaving line 289 as empty() since it only unlinks a pending op that was already authorized; (4) leave create_sem_set and the insert_at arm of get_or_create_sem_set unchecked, matching ipcget_new. Regressions to guard: subtest 2 must stay EEXIST and subtests 3-6 must keep ENOENT/EINVAL - all run as root, which the CAP_IPC_OWNER exemption must continue to wave through; and semget01/semctl/semop tests already enabled in all.txt exercise the same sets as their own creator, where the owner triplet of a mode 0600 set grants READ|ALTER, so they must not start failing.
